question: Count orders in each status. Return status and order count, sorted alphabetically by status.
expected_sql:
SELECT status,
       COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM orders
GROUP BY status
ORDER BY status;

question: Which customer regions are present? Return each distinct region once, alphabetically.

Return every customer ID, name, and completed-order revenue rounded to two decimals, including zero for customers without completed sales. Use item quantities and historical unit prices. Sort by customer ID.
expected_sql:
SELECT c.id,
       c.name,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_price), 0), 2) AS revenue
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
AND o.status = 'completed'
LEFT JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id
GROUP BY c.id,
         c.name

question: Which three products sold the most units in completed orders? Return product ID, name, and units. Exclude products without completed item lines; sort units descending, then product ID ascending.
expected_sql:
SELECT p.id,
       p.name,
       SUM(i.quantity) AS units
FROM products p
JOIN order_items i ON i.product_id = p.id
JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id
WHERE o.status = 'completed'
GROUP BY p.id,
         p.name
ORDER BY units DESC,
         p.id
LIMIT 3;

question: Which completed orders have an item total strictly above 100? Return order ID and total rounded to two decimals, sorted by order ID. Calculate totals from quantity times historical unit price.
expected_sql:
SELECT o.id,
       ROUND(SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_price), 2) AS order_total
FROM orders o
JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id
WHERE o.status = 'completed'
GROUP BY o.id
HAVING SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_price) > 100
ORDER BY o.id;

question: Which customers have both a completed order and a cancelled order? Return customer ID and name once each, ordered by ID.
expected_sql:
SELECT c.id,
       c.name
FROM customers c
WHERE EXISTS
        (SELECT 1
         FROM orders o
         WHERE o.customer_id = c.id
             AND o.status = 'completed')
    AND EXISTS
        (SELECT 1
         FROM orders o
         WHERE o.customer_id = c.id
             AND o.status = 'cancelled')
ORDER BY c.id;

question: For each month with completed orders, return YYYY-MM, revenue rounded to two decimals, and percentage change from the previous month present in the result, rounded to two decimals. Revenue uses historical item prices; empty orders contribute zero. Return NULL for the first change or a zero prior revenue. Sort by month.
expected_sql:
WITH monthly AS
    (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', o.ordered_at) AS MONTH,
            COALESCE(SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_price), 0) AS revenue
     FROM orders o
     LEFT JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id
     WHERE o.status = 'completed'
     GROUP BY MONTH),
     changes AS
    (SELECT MONTH,
            revenue,
            LAG(revenue) OVER (
                               ORDER BY MONTH) AS previous_revenue
     FROM monthly)
SELECT MONTH,
       ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue,
       ROUND(100.0 * (revenue - previous_revenue) / NULLIF(previous_revenue, 0), 2) AS growth_pct
FROM changes
ORDER BY MONTH;

question: Find the product or products with the highest completed-order revenue within each category, including ties. Include all catalog products in the comparison with zero revenue when unsold. Return category, product ID, name, and revenue rounded to two decimals; sort category then product ID. Use historical item prices.
expected_sql:
WITH totals AS
    (SELECT p.id,
            p.name,
            p.category,
            COALESCE(SUM(CASE
                             WHEN o.status = 'completed' THEN i.quantity * i.unit_price
                             ELSE 0
                         END), 0) AS revenue
     FROM products p
     LEFT JOIN order_items i ON i.product_id = p.id
     LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id
     GROUP BY p.id,
              p.name,
              p.category),
     ranked AS
    (SELECT *,
            DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category
                               ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS POSITION
     FROM totals)
SELECT category,
       id,
       name,
       ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue
FROM ranked
WHERE POSITION = 1
ORDER BY category,
         id;

question: Which customers have bought every catalog product in the Home category through completed orders? Require the Home category to contain at least one product. Return customer ID and name, ordered by ID.

question: Trace the reporting chain above employee 7. Return manager employee ID, manager name, and distance, where the direct manager is distance 1. Exclude employee 7; sort by distance ascending.
expected_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE chain(id, name, manager_id, distance) AS
    (SELECT m.id,
            m.name,
            m.manager_id,
            1
     FROM employees e
     JOIN employees m ON m.id = e.manager_id
     WHERE e.id = 7
     UNION ALL SELECT m.id,
                      m.name,
                      m.manager_id,
                      c.distance + 1
     FROM CHAIN c
     JOIN employees m ON m.id = c.manager_id)
SELECT id,
       name,
       distance
FROM CHAIN
ORDER BY distance;

question: Within each non-NULL department, return employees in the top two distinct salary levels, including everyone tied at either level. Return department ID, employee ID, name, salary, and dense salary rank. Sort by department ID, rank, then employee ID.
expected_sql:
WITH ranked AS
    (SELECT department_id,
            id,
            name,
            salary,
            DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id
                               ORDER BY salary DESC) AS salary_rank
     FROM employees
     WHERE department_id IS NOT NULL)
SELECT department_id,
       id,
       name,
       salary,
       salary_rank
FROM ranked
WHERE salary_rank <= 2
ORDER BY department_id,
         salary_rank,
         id;

question: For each employee assigned to a department, return department ID, employee ID, name, all-time logged hours, and percentage of that department's logged hours rounded to two decimals. Include employees with zero hours; return 0 percent when a department has no hours. Sort by department ID then employee ID.
expected_sql:
WITH totals AS
    (SELECT e.department_id,
            e.id,
            e.name,
            COALESCE(SUM(w.hours), 0) AS hours
     FROM employees e
     LEFT JOIN work_logs w ON w.employee_id = e.id
     WHERE e.department_id IS NOT NULL
     GROUP BY e.id,
              e.department_id,
              e.name)
SELECT department_id,
       id,
       name,
       hours,
       COALESCE(ROUND(100.0 * hours / NULLIF(SUM(hours) OVER (PARTITION BY department_id), 0), 2), 0) AS percentage
FROM totals
ORDER BY department_id,
         id;

question: For every student, return student ID, name, and credit-weighted average score rounded to two decimals across completed enrollments with a non-NULL score. Count repeat completions separately. Return NULL when no eligible grades exist. Sort by student ID.

question: Which students have completed every required course in their own major in any term? Exclude majors with no required courses. Return student ID and name, sorted by ID.
expected_sql:

WHERE EXISTS

question: For each term, find the course or courses with the highest average score among completed enrollments with non-NULL scores, retaining ties before rounding. Return term, course ID, title, and average score rounded to two decimals; sort by term then course ID.
expected_sql:
WITH averages AS
    (SELECT term,
            course_id,
            AVG(score) AS average_score
     FROM enrollments
     WHERE status = 'completed'
         AND score IS NOT NULL
     GROUP BY term,
              course_id),
     ranked AS
    (SELECT *,
            RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY term
                         ORDER BY average_score DESC) AS POSITION
     FROM averages)
SELECT r.term,
       c.id,
       c.title,
       ROUND(r.average_score, 2) AS average_score
FROM ranked r
JOIN courses c ON c.id = r.course_id
WHERE r.position = 1
ORDER BY r.term,
         c.id;

question: Among distinct students with a non-withdrawn enrollment in 2024-Fall, how many also have a non-withdrawn enrollment in 2025-Spring? Return one row with cohort student count, retained student count, and retention percent rounded to two decimals. A student counts once per group; return NULL percent for an empty cohort.
expected_sql:
WITH cohort AS
    (SELECT DISTINCT student_id
     FROM enrollments
     WHERE term = '2024-Fall'
         AND status <> 'withdrawn'),
     retained AS
    (SELECT student_id
     FROM cohort
     WHERE EXISTS
             (SELECT 1
              FROM enrollments e
              WHERE e.student_id = cohort.student_id
                  AND e.term = '2025-Spring'
                  AND e.status <> 'withdrawn'))
SELECT
    (SELECT COUNT(*)
     FROM cohort) AS cohort_count,

    (SELECT COUNT(*)
     FROM retained) AS retained_count,
       ROUND(100.0 *
                 (SELECT COUNT(*)
                  FROM retained) / NULLIF(
                                              (SELECT COUNT(*)
                                               FROM cohort), 0), 2) AS retention_pct;

question: For loans active at the end of 2025-06-30 whose due date is strictly earlier than that date, return loan ID, member name, book title, and integer days overdue as of 2025-06-30. A return after that date still counts as active. Sort by loan ID.
expected_sql:
SELECT l.id,
       m.name,
       b.title,
       CAST(julianday('2025-06-30') - julianday(l.due_at) AS INTEGER) AS days_overdue
FROM loans l
JOIN members m ON m.id = l.member_id
JOIN books b ON b.id = l.book_id
WHERE l.loaned_at <= '2025-06-30'
    AND (l.returned_at IS NULL
         OR l.returned_at > '2025-06-30')
    AND l.due_at < '2025-06-30'
ORDER BY l.id;

question: For every member, return member ID, name, returned-loan count, and average loan duration in days rounded to two decimals. Use all loans with a recorded return, including July returns. Return zero count and NULL average when none are returned; sort by member ID.
expected_sql:
SELECT m.id,
       m.name,
       COUNT(l.id) AS returned_count,
       ROUND(AVG(julianday(l.returned_at) - julianday(l.loaned_at)), 2) AS average_days
FROM members m
LEFT JOIN loans l ON l.member_id = m.id
AND l.returned_at IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY m.id,
         m.name
ORDER BY m.id;

question: Find all book titles tied for the highest number of loan records across all dates. Exclude titles never borrowed. Return book ID, title, and loan count; order by book ID.
expected_sql:
WITH counts AS
    (SELECT b.id,
            b.title,
            COUNT(*) AS loan_count
     FROM books b
     JOIN loans l ON l.book_id = b.id
     GROUP BY b.id,
              b.title)
SELECT id,
       title,
       loan_count
FROM counts
WHERE loan_count =
        (SELECT MAX(loan_count)
         FROM counts)
ORDER BY id;

question: Which members have borrowed titles from at least two different authors across all dates? Return member ID and name, ordered by member ID.

       m.name
FROM members m
WHERE m.id IN

         JOIN books b ON b.id = l.book_id
         GROUP BY l.member_id

question: For each loan, return member ID, loan ID, loan date, and integer days since that member's previous loan date. Order a member's loans by loan date then loan ID, and use NULL for the first loan. Sort the result by member ID, loan date, then loan ID.
expected_sql:
SELECT member_id,
       id,
       loaned_at,
       CAST(julianday(loaned_at) - julianday(LAG(loaned_at) OVER (PARTITION BY member_id
                                                                  ORDER BY loaned_at, id)) AS INTEGER) AS gap_days
FROM loans
ORDER BY member_id,
         loaned_at,
         id;

question: For each book, return book ID, title, and copies available at the end of 2025-06-30. Subtract loans started on or before that date and not returned by that date from total copies. Include titles with no active loans; order by book ID.
expected_sql:
SELECT b.id,
       b.title,
       b.total_copies - COUNT(l.id) AS available_copies
FROM books b
LEFT JOIN loans l ON l.book_id = b.id
AND l.loaned_at <= '2025-06-30'
AND (l.returned_at IS NULL
     OR l.returned_at > '2025-06-30')
GROUP BY b.id,
         b.title,
         b.total_copies
ORDER BY b.id;

question: Return each distinct tracking-event type in uppercase with underscores replaced by spaces, sorted alphabetically by the formatted value.
Which delivered shipments arrived strictly after their promised timestamp? Return shipment ID, customer name, and hours late rounded to two decimals; sort by shipment ID.
expected_sql:

       c.name,
       ROUND((julianday(s.delivered_at) - julianday(s.promised_at)) * 24, 2) AS hours_late

JOIN customers c ON c.id = s.customer_id
WHERE s.status = 'delivered'
    AND s.delivered_at > s.promised_at
ORDER BY s.id;

question: For every carrier, return carrier ID, name, and total cost divided by total weight of its non-cancelled shipments, rounded to two decimals. Return NULL when total weight is zero or no eligible shipments exist. Sort by carrier ID.

question: Which customers have used at least two different non-NULL carriers on non-cancelled shipments? Return customer ID, name, and distinct carrier count; sort by customer ID.

       COUNT(DISTINCT s.carrier_id) AS carrier_count

question: Which non-cancelled shipments have no tracking events? Return shipment ID and customer name, ordered by shipment ID.
expected_sql:

FROM shipments s
JOIN customers c ON c.id = s.customer_id
WHERE s.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND NOT EXISTS
        (SELECT 1
         FROM tracking_events e
         WHERE e.shipment_id = s.id)
ORDER BY s.id;

question: For every shipment, return shipment ID, latest event type, and latest event timestamp. Choose the highest event ID when timestamps tie; return NULL event fields when no events exist. Sort by shipment ID.
expected_sql:
WITH ranked AS
    (SELECT *,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY shipment_id
                               ORDER BY occurred_at DESC, id DESC) AS POSITION
     FROM tracking_events)
SELECT s.id,
       e.event_type,
       e.occurred_at
FROM shipments s
LEFT JOIN ranked e ON e.shipment_id = s.id
AND e.position = 1
ORDER BY s.id;

question: For shipments with both picked_up and delivered tracking events, return shipment ID and hours from the first picked_up event to the first delivered event rounded to two decimals. Use event timestamps, not shipment timestamps; sort by shipment ID.
expected_sql:
SELECT shipment_id,
       ROUND((julianday(MIN(CASE
                                WHEN event_type = 'delivered' THEN occurred_at
                            END)) - julianday(MIN(CASE
                                                      WHEN event_type = 'picked_up' THEN occurred_at
                                                  END))) * 24, 2) AS hours_elapsed
FROM tracking_events
GROUP BY shipment_id
HAVING COUNT(CASE
                 WHEN event_type = 'picked_up' THEN 1
             END) > 0
AND COUNT(CASE
              WHEN event_type = 'delivered' THEN 1
          END) > 0
ORDER BY shipment_id;

question: For each non-NULL carrier and each shipping date with non-cancelled shipments, return carrier ID, shipping date as YYYY-MM-DD, daily shipped weight, and cumulative shipped weight through that date for the carrier. Do not add missing dates. Sort by carrier ID then date.
expected_sql:
WITH daily AS
    (SELECT carrier_id,
            date(shipped_at) AS shipped_date,
            SUM(weight_kg) AS daily_weight
     FROM shipments
     WHERE carrier_id IS NOT NULL
         AND status <> 'cancelled'
     GROUP BY carrier_id,
              date(shipped_at))
SELECT carrier_id,
       shipped_date,
       daily_weight,
       SUM(daily_weight) OVER (PARTITION BY carrier_id
                               ORDER BY shipped_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_weight
FROM daily
ORDER BY carrier_id,
         shipped_date;

question: Find clinicians with at least two completed appointments. Return clinician_id, name, completed_count, and average completed-appointment fee rounded to two decimals. Order by clinician_id.

question: For every completed appointment, return appointment_id, patient name, fee, total payments, and balance_due. Balance is fee minus payments; keep negative balances for overpayments and use zero payments when none exist. Round payments and balance to two decimals and order by appointment_id.
expected_sql:
SELECT a.appointment_id,
       p.name,
       a.fee,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(pay.amount), 0), 2) AS total_payments,
       ROUND(a.fee - COALESCE(SUM(pay.amount), 0), 2) AS balance_due
FROM appointments a
JOIN patients p ON p.patient_id = a.patient_id
LEFT JOIN payments pay ON pay.appointment_id = a.appointment_id
WHERE a.status = 'completed'
GROUP BY a.appointment_id,
         p.name,
         a.fee
ORDER BY a.appointment_id;

question: Show every clinician, including clinicians without completed appointments, with clinician_id, name, and completed_count. Count only completed appointments and order by clinician_id.
expected_sql:
SELECT c.clinician_id,
       c.name,
       COUNT(a.appointment_id) AS completed_count
FROM appointments a
RIGHT JOIN clinicians c ON a.clinician_id = c.clinician_id
AND a.status = 'completed'
GROUP BY c.clinician_id,
         c.name
ORDER BY c.clinician_id;

question: Produce a reconciliation list containing every appointment and every payment, matching payments to appointments when possible. Keep one row per matched payment, appointments with no payment, and unallocated payments. Return appointment_id, payment_id, and amount; leave missing values NULL. Order by appointment_id with NULLs last, then payment_id.
expected_sql:
SELECT a.appointment_id,
       p.payment_id,
       p.amount
FROM appointments a
FULL OUTER JOIN payments p ON p.appointment_id = a.appointment_id
ORDER BY a.appointment_id IS NULL,
                             a.appointment_id,
                             p.payment_id;

question: Within each specialty, find the completed appointment or appointments with the highest fee, including ties. Return specialty, appointment_id, and fee, ordered by specialty and then appointment_id.
expected_sql:
WITH ranked AS
    (SELECT c.specialty,
            a.appointment_id,
            a.fee,
            DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.specialty
                               ORDER BY a.fee DESC) AS fee_rank
     FROM appointments a
     JOIN clinicians c ON c.clinician_id = a.clinician_id
     WHERE a.status = 'completed')
SELECT specialty,
       appointment_id,
       fee
FROM ranked
WHERE fee_rank = 1
ORDER BY specialty,
         appointment_id;

question: Which patients have at least one completed appointment and have fully paid every completed appointment? An appointment is fully paid when its summed payments are at least its fee; missing payments count as zero. Ignore appointments of other statuses. Return patient_id and name, ordered by patient_id.
expected_sql:
SELECT p.patient_id,
       p.name
FROM patients p
WHERE EXISTS
        (SELECT 1
         FROM appointments a
         WHERE a.patient_id = p.patient_id
             AND a.status = 'completed')
    AND NOT EXISTS
        (SELECT 1
         FROM appointments a
         WHERE a.patient_id = p.patient_id
             AND a.status = 'completed'
             AND COALESCE(
                              (SELECT SUM(pay.amount)
                               FROM payments pay
                               WHERE pay.appointment_id = a.appointment_id), 0) < a.fee)
ORDER BY p.patient_id;

question: List open checking accounts. Return account_id and account_number, ordered by account_id.
expected_sql:
SELECT account_id,
       account_number
FROM accounts
WHERE status = 'open'
    AND kind = 'checking'
ORDER BY account_id;

question: List withdrawal entries posted during March 2025. Return entry_id, account_id, posted_at, and the signed amount, ordered by posted_at and then entry_id.
expected_sql:
SELECT entry_id,
       account_id,
       posted_at,
       amount
FROM ledger_entries
WHERE entry_type = 'withdrawal'
    AND posted_at >= '2025-03-01'
    AND posted_at < '2025-04-01'
ORDER BY posted_at,
         entry_id;

question: Across all ledger entries, show each entry_type, its entry count, and the sum of signed amounts rounded to two decimals. Order by entry_type.
expected_sql:
SELECT entry_type,
       COUNT(*) AS entry_count,
       ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS signed_total
FROM ledger_entries
GROUP BY entry_type
ORDER BY entry_type;

question: For every customer, return customer_id, name, and the combined current balance of all their accounts, including closed accounts. Current balance is opening_balance plus all ledger entries. Customers without accounts should show zero. Round the combined balance to two decimals and order by customer_id.
expected_sql:
WITH account_balances AS
    (SELECT a.account_id,
            a.customer_id,
            a.opening_balance + COALESCE(SUM(l.amount), 0) AS balance
     FROM accounts a
     LEFT JOIN ledger_entries l ON l.account_id = a.account_id
     GROUP BY a.account_id,
              a.customer_id,
              a.opening_balance)
SELECT c.customer_id,
       c.name,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(b.balance), 0), 2) AS combined_balance
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN account_balances b ON b.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id,
         c.name
ORDER BY c.customer_id;

question: Find accounts with at least two negative ledger entries, including fees as well as withdrawals. Return account_number, negative_entry_count, and the positive total of money removed, rounded to two decimals. Use all posting dates and order by account_number.
expected_sql:
SELECT a.account_number,
       COUNT(*) AS negative_entry_count,
       ROUND(-SUM(l.amount), 2) AS money_removed
FROM accounts a
JOIN ledger_entries l ON l.account_id = a.account_id
WHERE l.amount < 0
GROUP BY a.account_id,
         a.account_number
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
ORDER BY a.account_number;

question: For every account, count ledger entries posted on or before March 31, 2025, and sum their signed amounts. Include accounts without qualifying entries with count zero and net change zero. Return account_number, entry_count, and net_change rounded to two decimals, ordered by account_number.
expected_sql:
SELECT a.account_number,
       COUNT(l.entry_id) AS entry_count,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(l.amount), 0), 2) AS net_change
FROM ledger_entries l
RIGHT JOIN accounts a ON a.account_id = l.account_id
AND l.posted_at < '2025-04-01'
GROUP BY a.account_id,
         a.account_number
ORDER BY a.account_number;

question: Compare each account with its March 31, 2025 statement when the statement ending balance is known. Show only mismatches after rounding both balances to two decimals. The book balance is opening_balance plus postings through March 31. Return account_number, book_balance, statement_balance, and the rounded book balance minus the rounded statement balance as difference. Round every monetary output to two decimals. Order by account_number ascending.
expected_sql:
WITH book AS
    (SELECT a.account_number,
            ROUND(a.opening_balance + COALESCE(SUM(l.amount), 0), 2) AS book_balance
     FROM accounts a
     LEFT JOIN ledger_entries l ON l.account_id = a.account_id
     AND l.posted_at < '2025-04-01'
     GROUP BY a.account_id,
              a.account_number,
              a.opening_balance)
SELECT b.account_number,
       b.book_balance,
       ROUND(s.ending_balance, 2) AS statement_balance,
       ROUND(b.book_balance - ROUND(s.ending_balance, 2), 2) AS difference
FROM book b
JOIN statements s ON s.account_number = b.account_number
WHERE s.statement_date = '2025-03-31'
    AND s.ending_balance IS NOT NULL
    AND b.book_balance <> ROUND(s.ending_balance, 2)
ORDER BY b.account_number;

question: Reconcile all local accounts with all imported statements dated March 31, 2025, retaining unmatched records on either side. Return account_number, book_balance, statement_balance, and the rounded book balance minus the rounded statement balance as difference. Book balance uses opening_balance plus postings through March 31. Round monetary outputs to two decimals; use NULL for a missing book balance, a missing or unknown statement balance, and any difference involving NULL. Order by account_number ascending.
expected_sql:
WITH book AS
    (SELECT a.account_number,
            ROUND(a.opening_balance + COALESCE(SUM(l.amount), 0), 2) AS book_balance
     FROM accounts a
     LEFT JOIN ledger_entries l ON l.account_id = a.account_id
     AND l.posted_at < '2025-04-01'
     GROUP BY a.account_id,
              a.account_number,
              a.opening_balance),
     imported AS
    (SELECT account_number,
            ending_balance
     FROM statements
     WHERE statement_date = '2025-03-31')
SELECT COALESCE(b.account_number, s.account_number) AS account_number,
       b.book_balance,
       ROUND(s.ending_balance, 2) AS statement_balance,
       ROUND(b.book_balance - ROUND(s.ending_balance, 2), 2) AS difference
FROM book b
FULL OUTER JOIN imported s ON s.account_number = b.account_number
ORDER BY account_number;

question: Show every ledger entry with its account running balance, starting from the account opening balance. Within an account, apply entries in posted_at then entry_id order, including all dates. Return account_number, entry_id, posted_at, and running_balance rounded to two decimals. Order the output by account_number, posted_at, and entry_id.
expected_sql:
SELECT a.account_number,
       l.entry_id,
       l.posted_at,
       ROUND(a.opening_balance + SUM(l.amount) OVER (PARTITION BY a.account_id
                                                     ORDER BY l.posted_at, l.entry_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS running_balance
FROM accounts a
JOIN ledger_entries l ON l.account_id = a.account_id
ORDER BY a.account_number,
         l.posted_at,
         l.entry_id;

question: Find open accounts whose current balance is strictly below the average current balance of open accounts of the same kind. Current balance includes opening_balance and all postings; include accounts with no entries in the comparison. Compare unrounded balances. Return account_number, kind, and current_balance rounded to two decimals, ordered by account_number.
expected_sql:
WITH balances AS
    (SELECT a.account_id,
            a.account_number,
            a.kind,
            a.opening_balance + COALESCE(SUM(l.amount), 0) AS balance
     FROM accounts a
     LEFT JOIN ledger_entries l ON l.account_id = a.account_id
     WHERE a.status = 'open'
     GROUP BY a.account_id,
              a.account_number,
              a.kind,
              a.opening_balance)
SELECT b.account_number,
       b.kind,
       ROUND(b.balance, 2) AS current_balance
FROM balances b
WHERE b.balance <
        (SELECT AVG(other.balance)
         FROM balances other
         WHERE other.kind = b.kind)
ORDER BY b.account_number;

question: List active subscriptions. Return subscription_id, customer_id, plan_id, and start_date, ordered by start_date and then subscription_id.
expected_sql:
SELECT subscription_id,
       customer_id,
       plan_id,
       start_date
FROM subscriptions
WHERE status = 'active'
ORDER BY start_date,
         subscription_id;

question: Which open invoices have an amount of at least 50? Return invoice_id, billed_on, and amount, ordered by amount descending and then invoice_id.
expected_sql:
SELECT invoice_id,
       billed_on,
       amount
FROM invoices
WHERE status = 'open'
    AND amount >= 50
ORDER BY amount DESC,
         invoice_id;

question: Show paid invoice revenue by billing month, using the historical invoice amounts. Return month as YYYY-MM and revenue rounded to two decimals. Include only months with paid invoices and order chronologically.
expected_sql:
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', billed_on) AS MONTH,
       ROUND(SUM(amount), 2) AS revenue
FROM invoices
WHERE status = 'paid'
GROUP BY MONTH
ORDER BY MONTH;

question: For every customer, return customer_id, name, and total paid invoice amount across all their subscriptions, regardless of subscription status. Include customers with no paid invoices as zero, round the total to two decimals, and order by customer_id.
expected_sql:
SELECT c.customer_id,
       c.name,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(i.amount), 0), 2) AS paid_total
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN invoices i ON i.subscription_id = s.subscription_id
AND i.status = 'paid'
GROUP BY c.customer_id,
         c.name
ORDER BY c.customer_id;

question: For every plan, including plans with no active subscriptions, return plan_id, name, and active_subscription_count. Count status active only and order by plan_id.
expected_sql:
SELECT p.plan_id,
       p.name,
       COUNT(s.subscription_id) AS active_subscription_count
FROM subscriptions s
RIGHT JOIN plans p ON p.plan_id = s.plan_id
AND s.status = 'active'
GROUP BY p.plan_id,
         p.name
ORDER BY p.plan_id;

question: Which subscriptions exceeded their plan included_units allowance during January 2025? Ignore subscription status. Return subscription_id, plan name, January units used, and units above the allowance. Include only positive overages and order by subscription_id.
expected_sql:
SELECT s.subscription_id,
       p.name,
       SUM(u.units) AS units_used,
       SUM(u.units) - p.included_units AS overage_units
FROM subscriptions s
JOIN plans p ON p.plan_id = s.plan_id
JOIN usage_events u ON u.subscription_id = s.subscription_id
WHERE u.used_on >= '2025-01-01'
    AND u.used_on < '2025-02-01'
GROUP BY s.subscription_id,
         p.name,
         p.included_units
HAVING SUM(u.units) > p.included_units
ORDER BY s.subscription_id;

question: Find customers whose open invoices total at least 50 across all subscriptions. Return customer_id, name, open_invoice_count, and open_amount rounded to two decimals, ordered by customer_id. Exclude paid and void invoices.
expected_sql:
SELECT c.customer_id,
       c.name,
       COUNT(i.invoice_id) AS open_invoice_count,
       ROUND(SUM(i.amount), 2) AS open_amount
FROM customers c
JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN invoices i ON i.subscription_id = s.subscription_id
WHERE i.status = 'open'
GROUP BY c.customer_id,
         c.name
HAVING SUM(i.amount) >= 50
ORDER BY c.customer_id;

question: Find subscriptions that have at least one usage event but have never had an invoice of any status. Return subscription_id, customer name, and plan name, ordered by subscription_id.
expected_sql:
SELECT s.subscription_id,
       c.name AS customer_name,
       p.name AS plan_name
FROM subscriptions s
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
JOIN plans p ON p.plan_id = s.plan_id
WHERE EXISTS
        (SELECT 1
         FROM usage_events u
         WHERE u.subscription_id = s.subscription_id)
    AND NOT EXISTS
        (SELECT 1
         FROM invoices i
         WHERE i.subscription_id = s.subscription_id)
ORDER BY s.subscription_id;

question: Show each paid invoice together with the running paid revenue for its customer across all subscriptions. Apply invoices in billed_on then invoice_id order within each customer. Return customer_id, invoice_id, billed_on, and running_paid_amount rounded to two decimals. Order by customer_id, billed_on, and invoice_id.
expected_sql:
SELECT s.customer_id,
       i.invoice_id,
       i.billed_on,
       ROUND(SUM(i.amount) OVER (PARTITION BY s.customer_id
                                 ORDER BY i.billed_on, i.invoice_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS running_paid_amount
FROM invoices i
JOIN subscriptions s ON s.subscription_id = i.subscription_id
WHERE i.status = 'paid'
ORDER BY s.customer_id,
         i.billed_on,
         i.invoice_id;

question: Which customers have at least one subscription and have at least one paid invoice for every subscription they have ever held, including cancelled or paused subscriptions? Return customer_id and name, ordered by customer_id.
expected_sql:
SELECT c.customer_id,
       c.name
FROM customers c
WHERE EXISTS
        (SELECT 1
         FROM subscriptions s
         WHERE s.customer_id = c.customer_id)
    AND NOT EXISTS
        (SELECT 1
         FROM subscriptions s
         WHERE s.customer_id = c.customer_id
             AND NOT EXISTS
                 (SELECT 1
                  FROM invoices i
                  WHERE i.subscription_id = s.subscription_id
                      AND i.status = 'paid'))
ORDER BY c.customer_id;

question: Which high-priority tickets currently have status open? Return ticket_id, opened_at, and assigned_agent_id, retaining NULL for unassigned tickets. Sort by opened_at ascending, then ticket_id ascending.
expected_sql:
SELECT ticket_id,
       opened_at,
       assigned_agent_id
FROM tickets
WHERE priority = 'high'
    AND status = 'open'
ORDER BY opened_at,
         ticket_id;

question: Count closed tickets for each priority that has at least one closed ticket. Return priority and closed_ticket_count, sorted by priority alphabetically.
expected_sql:
SELECT priority,
       COUNT(*) AS closed_ticket_count
FROM tickets
WHERE status = 'closed'
GROUP BY priority
ORDER BY priority;

question: List the agents in team 1. Return agent_id and name, sorted by name alphabetically, then agent_id ascending.
expected_sql:
SELECT agent_id,
       name
FROM agents
WHERE team_id = 1
ORDER BY name,
         agent_id;

question: For every team, count its unresolved tickets, meaning status open or pending, including tickets without an assigned agent. Include teams with zero unresolved tickets. Return team_id, team_name, and unresolved_ticket_count, sorted by team_id ascending.
expected_sql:
SELECT tm.team_id,
       tm.name AS team_name,
       COUNT(t.ticket_id) AS unresolved_ticket_count
FROM teams AS tm
LEFT JOIN tickets AS t ON t.team_id = tm.team_id
AND t.status IN ('open',
                 'pending')
GROUP BY tm.team_id,
         tm.name
ORDER BY tm.team_id;

question: For every customer, report the number of tickets of any status and the number of those tickets with no assigned agent. Include customers without tickets with both counts zero. Return customer_id, customer_name, ticket_count, and unassigned_ticket_count, sorted by customer_id ascending.
expected_sql:
SELECT c.customer_id,
       c.name AS customer_name,
       COUNT(t.ticket_id) AS ticket_count,
       SUM(CASE
               WHEN t.ticket_id IS NOT NULL
                    AND t.assigned_agent_id IS NULL THEN 1
               ELSE 0
           END) AS unassigned_ticket_count
FROM customers AS c
LEFT JOIN tickets AS t ON t.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id,
         c.name
ORDER BY c.customer_id;

question: For each ticket that has received an agent_reply event, find its earliest agent reply and the elapsed hours from opening to that reply. Ignore other event types. Return ticket_id, first_reply_at, and response_hours rounded to two decimal places, sorted by ticket_id ascending.
expected_sql:
SELECT t.ticket_id,
       MIN(e.created_at) AS first_reply_at,
       ROUND((julianday(MIN(e.created_at)) - julianday(t.opened_at)) * 24, 2) AS response_hours
FROM tickets AS t
INNER JOIN ticket_events AS e ON e.ticket_id = t.ticket_id
WHERE e.event_type = 'agent_reply'
GROUP BY t.ticket_id,
         t.opened_at
ORDER BY t.ticket_id;

question: Which agents are assigned at least two tickets with status closed? Return agent_id, agent_name, and closed_ticket_count. Sort by closed_ticket_count descending, then agent_id ascending.
expected_sql:
SELECT a.agent_id,
       a.name AS agent_name,
       COUNT(t.ticket_id) AS closed_ticket_count
FROM agents AS a
INNER JOIN tickets AS t ON t.assigned_agent_id = a.agent_id
WHERE t.status = 'closed'
GROUP BY a.agent_id,
         a.name
HAVING COUNT(t.ticket_id) >= 2
ORDER BY closed_ticket_count DESC,
         a.agent_id;

question: Find the oldest unresolved ticket, meaning status open or pending, for each team that has one. Exclude tickets without a team. If a team has several tickets opened at the same time, choose the lowest ticket_id. Return team_id, team_name, ticket_id, and opened_at, sorted by team_id ascending.
expected_sql:
WITH ranked AS
    (SELECT team_id,
            ticket_id,
            opened_at,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY team_id
                               ORDER BY opened_at, ticket_id) AS POSITION
     FROM tickets
     WHERE status IN ('open',
                      'pending')
         AND team_id IS NOT NULL)
SELECT tm.team_id,
       tm.name AS team_name,
       r.ticket_id,
       r.opened_at
FROM ranked AS r
INNER JOIN teams AS tm ON tm.team_id = r.team_id
WHERE r.position = 1
ORDER BY tm.team_id;

question: Build a complete assignment roster showing every ticket of any status with its assigned agent, every unassigned ticket with NULL agent fields, and every agent with no tickets with NULL ticket fields. Return agent_id, agent_name, ticket_id, and status. Sort by agent_id ascending with NULL agents last, then ticket_id ascending with NULL tickets last.
expected_sql:
SELECT a.agent_id,
       a.name AS agent_name,
       t.ticket_id,
       t.status
FROM tickets AS t
FULL OUTER JOIN agents AS a ON a.agent_id = t.assigned_agent_id
ORDER BY a.agent_id IS NULL,
                       a.agent_id,
                       t.ticket_id IS NULL,
                                      t.ticket_id;

question: For each team, identify all agents tied for the largest number of assigned unresolved tickets, meaning status open or pending. Exclude teams where every agent has zero assigned unresolved tickets. Count workload by the agent's team, and ignore unassigned tickets. Return team_id, team_name, agent_id, agent_name, and unresolved_ticket_count, sorted by team_id ascending, then agent_id ascending.
expected_sql:
WITH workloads AS
    (SELECT a.team_id,
            a.agent_id,
            a.name AS agent_name,
            COUNT(t.ticket_id) AS unresolved_ticket_count
     FROM agents AS a
     LEFT JOIN tickets AS t ON t.assigned_agent_id = a.agent_id
     AND t.status IN ('open',
                      'pending')
     GROUP BY a.team_id,
              a.agent_id,
              a.name),
     ranked AS
    (SELECT *,
            DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY team_id
                               ORDER BY unresolved_ticket_count DESC) AS POSITION
     FROM workloads)
SELECT tm.team_id,
       tm.name AS team_name,
       r.agent_id,
       r.agent_name,
       r.unresolved_ticket_count
FROM ranked AS r
INNER JOIN teams AS tm ON tm.team_id = r.team_id
WHERE r.position = 1
    AND r.unresolved_ticket_count > 0
ORDER BY tm.team_id,
         r.agent_id;

question: Which rooms have a current nightly_rate of 160 or less? Return room_number, room_type, and nightly_rate. Sort by nightly_rate descending, then room_number ascending.
expected_sql:
SELECT room_number,
       room_type,
       nightly_rate
FROM rooms
WHERE nightly_rate <= 160
ORDER BY nightly_rate DESC,
         room_number;

question: List confirmed bookings whose check-in date falls in February or March 2025. Return booking_id, check_in, and check_out, sorted by check_in ascending, then booking_id ascending.
expected_sql:
SELECT booking_id,
       check_in,
       check_out
FROM bookings
WHERE status = 'confirmed'
    AND check_in >= '2025-02-01'
    AND check_in < '2025-04-01'
ORDER BY check_in,
         booking_id;

question: For each checked_out booking, calculate its number of nights and booking value using booked_nightly_rate. Checkout day is excluded. Return booking_id, nights as an integer, and booking_value rounded to two decimal places, sorted by booking_id ascending.
expected_sql:
SELECT booking_id,
       CAST(julianday(check_out) - julianday(check_in) AS INTEGER) AS nights,
       ROUND((julianday(check_out) - julianday(check_in)) * booked_nightly_rate, 2) AS booking_value
FROM bookings
WHERE status = 'checked_out'
ORDER BY booking_id;

question: For every room, count checked_out bookings and their total nights, excluding checkout days. Include rooms without checked_out bookings with both totals zero. Return room_id, room_number, completed_booking_count, and total_nights as an integer, sorted by room_number ascending.
expected_sql:
SELECT r.room_id,
       r.room_number,
       COUNT(b.booking_id) AS completed_booking_count,
       CAST(COALESCE(SUM(julianday(b.check_out) - julianday(b.check_in)), 0) AS INTEGER) AS total_nights
FROM bookings AS b
RIGHT JOIN rooms AS r ON r.room_id = b.room_id
AND b.status = 'checked_out'
GROUP BY r.room_id,
         r.room_number
ORDER BY r.room_number;

question: For every guest, total the booking value of their checked_out stays, using each booking's historical booked_nightly_rate multiplied by nights and excluding checkout days. Include guests with no checked_out stays with a zero total. Return guest_id, guest_name, and completed_booking_value rounded to two decimal places, sorted by guest_id ascending.
expected_sql:
SELECT g.guest_id,
       g.name AS guest_name,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM((julianday(b.check_out) - julianday(b.check_in)) * b.booked_nightly_rate), 0), 2) AS completed_booking_value
FROM guests AS g
LEFT JOIN bookings AS b ON b.guest_id = g.guest_id
AND b.status = 'checked_out'
GROUP BY g.guest_id,
         g.name
ORDER BY g.guest_id;

question: How much net cash has been received for checked_out bookings in each room type? Sum signed payments so refunds reduce the total; exclude payments for other booking statuses and unallocated payments. Only include room types with at least one qualifying payment. Return room_type and net_payments rounded to two decimal places, sorted by room_type alphabetically.
expected_sql:
SELECT r.room_type,
       ROUND(SUM(p.amount), 2) AS net_payments
FROM payments AS p
INNER JOIN bookings AS b ON b.booking_id = p.booking_id
INNER JOIN rooms AS r ON r.room_id = b.room_id
WHERE b.status = 'checked_out'
GROUP BY r.room_type
ORDER BY r.room_type;

question: Which checked_out bookings still have a positive outstanding balance? Balance equals nights excluding checkout day times booked_nightly_rate, minus all signed payments for that booking; treat no payments as zero. Return booking_id, guest_name, room_number, and outstanding_balance rounded to two decimal places, sorted by booking_id ascending. Test positivity before rounding.
expected_sql:
SELECT b.booking_id,
       g.name AS guest_name,
       r.room_number,
       ROUND((julianday(b.check_out) - julianday(b.check_in)) * b.booked_nightly_rate - COALESCE(SUM(p.amount), 0), 2) AS outstanding_balance
FROM bookings AS b
INNER JOIN guests AS g ON g.guest_id = b.guest_id
INNER JOIN rooms AS r ON r.room_id = b.room_id
LEFT JOIN payments AS p ON p.booking_id = b.booking_id
WHERE b.status = 'checked_out'
GROUP BY b.booking_id,
         g.name,
         r.room_number,
         b.check_in,
         b.check_out,
         b.booked_nightly_rate
HAVING (julianday(b.check_out) - julianday(b.check_in)) * b.booked_nightly_rate - COALESCE(SUM(p.amount), 0) > 0
ORDER BY b.booking_id;

question: Find overlapping pairs of bookings for the same room, considering only confirmed and checked_out bookings. A booking occupies [check_in, check_out), so a checkout on another booking's check-in date is not an overlap. Return each pair once, with the lower booking_id first. Return room_number, first_booking_id, and second_booking_id, sorted by room_number, first_booking_id, then second_booking_id, all ascending.
expected_sql:
SELECT r.room_number,
       a.booking_id AS first_booking_id,
       b.booking_id AS second_booking_id
FROM bookings AS a
INNER JOIN bookings AS b ON b.room_id = a.room_id
AND a.booking_id < b.booking_id
AND a.check_in < b.check_out
AND b.check_in < a.check_out
INNER JOIN rooms AS r ON r.room_id = a.room_id
WHERE a.status IN ('confirmed',
                   'checked_out')
    AND b.status IN ('confirmed',
                     'checked_out')
ORDER BY r.room_number,
         a.booking_id,
         b.booking_id;

question: Within each room type, find every room tied for the highest total booking value from checked_out stays. Use historical booked_nightly_rate times nights excluding checkout days, and assign zero to rooms without checked_out stays; if every room in a type has zero, return all of them. Return room_type, room_number, and completed_booking_value rounded to two decimal places. Rank using unrounded totals and sort by room_type alphabetically, then room_number ascending.
expected_sql:
WITH room_values AS
    (SELECT r.room_id,
            r.room_number,
            r.room_type,
            COALESCE(SUM((julianday(b.check_out) - julianday(b.check_in)) * b.booked_nightly_rate), 0) AS booking_value
     FROM rooms AS r
     LEFT JOIN bookings AS b ON b.room_id = r.room_id
     AND b.status = 'checked_out'
     GROUP BY r.room_id,
              r.room_number,
              r.room_type),
     ranked AS
    (SELECT *,
            DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY room_type
                               ORDER BY booking_value DESC) AS POSITION
     FROM room_values)
SELECT room_type,
       room_number,
       ROUND(booking_value, 2) AS completed_booking_value
FROM ranked
WHERE POSITION = 1
ORDER BY room_type,
         room_number;

question: Which guests have at least two checked_out stays and an average stay length strictly above the average length across all checked_out bookings? Compute nights excluding checkout day, and compare the unrounded averages; the overall average is per booking, not per guest. Return guest_id, guest_name, and average_nights rounded to two decimal places, sorted by guest_id ascending.
expected_sql:
WITH completed_stays AS
    (SELECT guest_id,
            julianday(check_out) - julianday(check_in) AS nights
     FROM bookings
     WHERE status = 'checked_out')
SELECT g.guest_id,
       g.name AS guest_name,
       ROUND(AVG(s.nights), 2) AS average_nights
FROM guests AS g
INNER JOIN completed_stays AS s ON s.guest_id = g.guest_id
GROUP BY g.guest_id,
         g.name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
AND AVG(s.nights) >
    (SELECT AVG(nights)
     FROM completed_stays)
ORDER BY g.guest_id;

question: For each part with at least one completed work order, show the total completed quantity and the number of distinct direct component parts in its bill of materials. question: For each completed work order, show the previous completed work order date for the same part and the integer calendar-day gap from it. question: Calculate the leaf-material requirements for building three Desk lamps (part_id 1). A leaf material is a descendant with no components of its own. Multiply quantities along each path, add quantities when a leaf appears along multiple paths, and price the resulting quantity at the leaf part's unit_cost. Return leaf_part_id, name, required_quantity, material_cost rounded to two decimal places, ordered by leaf_part_id ascending.
expected_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE requirements(part_id, required_quantity) AS
    (SELECT component_part_id,
            quantity * 3
     FROM bom
     WHERE parent_part_id = 1
     UNION ALL SELECT b.component_part_id,
                      r.required_quantity * b.quantity
     FROM requirements AS r
     JOIN bom AS b ON b.parent_part_id = r.part_id)
SELECT p.id AS leaf_part_id,
       p.name,
       SUM(r.required_quantity) AS required_quantity,
       ROUND(SUM(r.required_quantity) * p.unit_cost, 2) AS material_cost
FROM requirements AS r
JOIN parts AS p ON p.id = r.part_id
WHERE NOT EXISTS
        (SELECT 1
         FROM bom AS b
         WHERE b.parent_part_id = r.part_id)
GROUP BY p.id,
         p.name,
         p.unit_cost
ORDER BY p.id;

question: For every ancestor part that has components, list all its direct and indirect descendant parts. For one unit of the ancestor, multiply quantities along each path and add the quantities across all paths to the same descendant. Exclude the ancestor itself. Return ancestor_part_id, descendant_part_id, required_quantity, ordered by ancestor_part_id and then descendant_part_id ascending.
expected_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE paths(ancestor_part_id, descendant_part_id, required_quantity) AS
    (SELECT parent_part_id,
            component_part_id,
            quantity
     FROM bom
     UNION ALL SELECT p.ancestor_part_id,
                      b.component_part_id,
                      p.required_quantity * b.quantity
     FROM paths AS p
     JOIN bom AS b ON b.parent_part_id = p.descendant_part_id)
SELECT ancestor_part_id,
       descendant_part_id,
       SUM(required_quantity) AS required_quantity
FROM paths
WHERE ancestor_part_id <> descendant_part_id
GROUP BY ancestor_part_id,
         descendant_part_id
ORDER BY ancestor_part_id,
         descendant_part_id;

question: For every product, show total current on-hand units across warehouses and the net sum of all quantity changes recorded during January 2025. question: For each movement whose reason is outbound, show the date of the immediately following recorded movement for the same warehouse and product, considering all reasons when finding that following movement. Return movement_id, warehouse_id, product_id, movement_date, next_movement_date, gap_days as an integer calendar-day difference; use NULL for the final two columns if there is no later movement. ORDER BY movement_id;

question: Within each meter, sequence nonmissing readings by reading_at and then reading_id ascending and form intervals between consecutive nonmissing readings. Omit the first reading. Return meter_id, reading_id, reading_at, elapsed_hours rounded to two decimals, consumed_kwh as current minus previous reading rounded to two decimals, average_kw as consumed_kwh divided by elapsed hours rounded to three decimals. Use NULL average_kw for zero elapsed hours. Order by meter_id, reading_at, reading_id ascending.
expected_sql:
WITH previous AS
    (SELECT meter_id,
            id AS reading_id,
            reading_at,
            reading_kwh,
            LAG(reading_at) OVER (PARTITION BY meter_id
                                  ORDER BY reading_at, id) AS previous_at,
            LAG(reading_kwh) OVER (PARTITION BY meter_id
                                   ORDER BY reading_at, id) AS previous_kwh
     FROM readings
     WHERE reading_kwh IS NOT NULL),
     intervals AS
    (SELECT meter_id,
            reading_id,
            reading_at,
            (julianday(reading_at) - julianday(previous_at)) * 24 AS elapsed_hours,
            reading_kwh - previous_kwh AS consumed_kwh
     FROM previous
     WHERE previous_at IS NOT NULL)
SELECT meter_id,
       reading_id,
       reading_at,
       ROUND(elapsed_hours, 2) AS elapsed_hours,
       ROUND(consumed_kwh, 2) AS consumed_kwh,
       ROUND(consumed_kwh / NULLIF(elapsed_hours, 0), 3) AS average_kw
FROM intervals
ORDER BY meter_id,
         reading_at,
         reading_id;

question: For each meter, derive consumed kWh between consecutive nonmissing readings, sequencing by reading_at and then reading_id ascending. Omit the first reading because it has no preceding interval. For every remaining interval, calculate the arithmetic mean of its consumption and up to two preceding interval consumptions for that meter; divide by the number of available intervals, without time weighting. Return meter_id, reading_id, reading_at, consumed_kwh, trailing_mean_kwh, with both kWh outputs rounded to two decimals. Order by meter_id, reading_at, reading_id ascending.
expected_sql:
WITH previous AS
    (SELECT meter_id,
            id AS reading_id,
            reading_at,
            reading_kwh,
            LAG(reading_kwh) OVER (PARTITION BY meter_id
                                   ORDER BY reading_at, id) AS previous_kwh
     FROM readings
     WHERE reading_kwh IS NOT NULL),
     intervals AS
    (SELECT meter_id,
            reading_id,
            reading_at,
            reading_kwh - previous_kwh AS consumed_kwh
     FROM previous
     WHERE previous_kwh IS NOT NULL)
SELECT meter_id,
       reading_id,
       reading_at,
       ROUND(consumed_kwh, 2) AS consumed_kwh,
       ROUND(AVG(consumed_kwh) OVER (PARTITION BY meter_id
                                     ORDER BY reading_at, reading_id ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS trailing_mean_kwh
FROM intervals
ORDER BY meter_id,
         reading_at,
         reading_id;

question: Rank meters having at least two nonmissing readings by observed consumption, defined as maximum minus minimum reading, in descending order. Equal unrounded consumption values share a rank, and the next rank skips the number of tied positions. Return meter_id, label, observed_consumption_kwh rounded to two decimals, consumption_rank, ordered by consumption_rank and then meter_id ascending.
expected_sql:
WITH consumption AS

            MAX(r.reading_kwh) - MIN(r.reading_kwh) AS observed_consumption_kwh
     FROM meters AS m
     JOIN readings AS r ON r.meter_id = m.id

     HAVING COUNT(r.reading_kwh) >= 2)

       ROUND(observed_consumption_kwh, 2) AS observed_consumption_kwh,
       RANK() OVER (
                    ORDER BY observed_consumption_kwh DESC) AS consumption_rank
FROM consumption

question: For every route, report its number of completed trips and number of listed stop positions, counting each trip and each position once. Use zero for missing counts. Return route_id, name, completed_trip_count, stop_count, ordered by route_id ascending.
expected_sql:
WITH completed AS
    (SELECT route_id,
            COUNT(*) AS completed_trip_count
     FROM trips
     WHERE status = 'completed'
     GROUP BY route_id),
     stop_counts AS
    (SELECT route_id,
            COUNT(*) AS stop_count
     FROM route_stops
     GROUP BY route_id)
SELECT r.id AS route_id,
       r.name,
       COALESCE(c.completed_trip_count, 0) AS completed_trip_count,
       COALESCE(s.stop_count, 0) AS stop_count
FROM routes AS r
LEFT JOIN completed AS c ON c.route_id = r.id
LEFT JOIN stop_counts AS s ON s.route_id = r.id
ORDER BY r.id;

question: Show every pair of adjacent stop positions on the same route, where the destination sequence is exactly one greater than the origin sequence. Return route_id, origin_sequence, origin_stop, destination_stop, segment_minutes using the destination position's travel_minutes_from_previous. Order by route_id and then origin_sequence ascending.
expected_sql:
SELECT a.route_id,
       a.stop_sequence AS origin_sequence,
       origin.name AS origin_stop,
       destination.name AS destination_stop,
       b.travel_minutes_from_previous AS segment_minutes
FROM route_stops AS a
JOIN route_stops AS b ON b.route_id = a.route_id
AND b.stop_sequence = a.stop_sequence + 1
JOIN stops AS origin ON origin.id = a.stop_id
JOIN stops AS destination ON destination.id = b.stop_id
ORDER BY a.route_id,
         a.stop_sequence;

question: For every listed route stop, calculate planned elapsed travel minutes from the first stop through that position, treating a missing segment time as zero. Return route_id, stop_sequence, stop_name, elapsed_minutes, ordered by route_id and then stop_sequence ascending.
expected_sql:
SELECT rs.route_id,
       rs.stop_sequence,
       s.name AS stop_name,
       SUM(COALESCE(rs.travel_minutes_from_previous, 0)) OVER (PARTITION BY rs.route_id
                                                               ORDER BY rs.stop_sequence ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS elapsed_minutes
FROM route_stops AS rs
JOIN stops AS s ON s.id = rs.stop_id
ORDER BY rs.route_id,
         rs.stop_sequence;

question: For every route with a completed trip, return exactly its latest completed trip, choosing by service_date descending, then scheduled_departure descending, then trip_id descending. Return route_id, trip_id, service_date, actual_departure, ordered by route_id ascending.
expected_sql:
WITH ordered AS
    (SELECT route_id,
            id AS trip_id,
            service_date,
            actual_departure,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY route_id
                               ORDER BY service_date DESC, scheduled_departure DESC, id DESC) AS POSITION
     FROM trips
     WHERE status = 'completed')
SELECT route_id,
       trip_id,
       service_date,
       actual_departure
FROM ordered
WHERE POSITION = 1
ORDER BY route_id;

question: Within each route, divide completed trips in chronological order into two batches of sizes differing by at most one. Order trips by service_date, scheduled_departure, and trip_id ascending; batch 1 contains the earlier trips and gets the extra trip when the count is odd. A route with one completed trip uses only batch 1. Return route_id, trip_id, service_date, batch_number, ordered by route_id, service_date, scheduled_departure, trip_id ascending.
expected_sql:
SELECT route_id,
       id AS trip_id,
       service_date,
       NTILE(2) OVER (PARTITION BY route_id
                      ORDER BY service_date, scheduled_departure, id) AS batch_number
FROM trips
WHERE status = 'completed'
ORDER BY route_id,
         service_date,
         scheduled_departure,
         id;

question: For each session referrer, using direct for NULL, report the number of sessions, the number of sessions containing at least one purchase event, and total purchase-event revenue. Count each session once even when it contains multiple events, retain sessions without events, and use zero revenue when there are no purchases. Return referrer, session_count, converting_session_count, purchase_revenue rounded to two decimals, ordered by referrer alphabetically.
expected_sql:
SELECT COALESCE(s.referrer, 'direct') AS referrer,
       COUNT(DISTINCT s.id) AS session_count,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE
                          WHEN e.event_type = 'purchase' THEN s.id
                      END) AS converting_session_count,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(CASE
                              WHEN e.event_type = 'purchase' THEN e.revenue
                              ELSE 0
                          END), 0), 2) AS purchase_revenue
FROM sessions AS s
LEFT JOIN EVENTS AS e ON e.session_id = s.id
GROUP BY COALESCE(s.referrer, 'direct')
ORDER BY referrer;

question: For every session, count its events and calculate the span in whole seconds from its earliest to latest event. Return NULL span for a session with no events and zero for one event. Return session_id, event_count, event_span_seconds, ordered by session_id ascending.
expected_sql:
SELECT s.id AS session_id,
       COUNT(e.id) AS event_count,
       CAST(ROUND((julianday(MAX(e.event_at)) - julianday(MIN(e.event_at))) * 86400) AS INTEGER) AS event_span_seconds
FROM sessions AS s
LEFT JOIN EVENTS AS e ON e.session_id = s.id
GROUP BY s.id
ORDER BY s.id;

question: For each visitor country with at least one session, calculate its session conversion rate: 100 times the number of sessions containing at least one purchase event divided by all sessions from that country. A session with multiple purchase events counts once. Return country, session_count, converting_session_count, conversion_percent rounded to two decimals, ordered by country alphabetically.
expected_sql:
WITH session_flags AS
    (SELECT s.id AS session_id,
            v.country,
            MAX(CASE
                    WHEN e.event_type = 'purchase' THEN 1
                    ELSE 0
                END) AS converted
     FROM sessions AS s
     JOIN visitors AS v ON v.id = s.visitor_id
     LEFT JOIN EVENTS AS e ON e.session_id = s.id
     GROUP BY s.id,
              v.country)
SELECT country,
       COUNT(*) AS session_count,
       SUM(converted) AS converting_session_count,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(converted) / COUNT(*), 2) AS conversion_percent
FROM session_flags
GROUP BY country
ORDER BY country;

question: For every session, show the previous session start for the same visitor and the elapsed hours since it. Sequence each visitor's sessions by started_at and then session_id ascending, including ties in start time. The first session has NULL for the previous start and gap. Return visitor_id, session_id, started_at, previous_started_at, gap_hours rounded to two decimals, ordered by visitor_id, started_at, session_id ascending.
expected_sql:
WITH previous AS
    (SELECT visitor_id,
            id AS session_id,
            started_at,
            LAG(started_at) OVER (PARTITION BY visitor_id
                                  ORDER BY started_at, id) AS previous_started_at
     FROM sessions)
SELECT visitor_id,
       session_id,
       started_at,
       previous_started_at,
       ROUND((julianday(started_at) - julianday(previous_started_at)) * 24, 2) AS gap_hours
FROM previous
ORDER BY visitor_id,
         started_at,
         session_id;

question: For each UTC calendar day from 2025-01-01 through 2025-01-04 inclusive, show purchase-event revenue, cumulative revenue since 2025-01-01, and the arithmetic mean of that day's and the preceding calendar day's revenue within this reporting period. Include days without purchases as zero; the first day's mean uses only that day. Return day formatted YYYY-MM-DD, purchase_revenue, cumulative_revenue, two_day_mean_revenue, with all revenue values rounded to two decimals, ordered by day ascending.
expected_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE calendar(DAY) AS
    (SELECT '2025-01-01'
     UNION ALL SELECT DATE(DAY, '+1 day')
     FROM calendar
     WHERE DAY < '2025-01-04'),
               revenue AS
    (SELECT DATE(event_at) AS DAY,
            SUM(revenue) AS purchase_revenue
     FROM EVENTS
     WHERE event_type = 'purchase'
         AND event_at >= '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
         AND event_at < '2025-01-05 00:00:00'
     GROUP BY DATE(event_at)),
               daily AS
    (SELECT c.day,
            COALESCE(r.purchase_revenue, 0) AS purchase_revenue
     FROM calendar AS c
     LEFT JOIN revenue AS r ON r.day = c.day)
SELECT DAY,
       ROUND(purchase_revenue, 2) AS purchase_revenue,
       ROUND(SUM(purchase_revenue) OVER (
                                         ORDER BY DAY ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS cumulative_revenue,
       ROUND(AVG(purchase_revenue) OVER (
                                         ORDER BY DAY ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS two_day_mean_revenue
FROM daily
ORDER BY DAY;

question: For every visitor, total their purchase-event revenue, using zero for visitors without purchases or sessions. Rank visitors by unrounded revenue ascending with equal revenues sharing the first position occupied by that tie group, and calculate percentile_fraction as (rank minus one) divided by (number of visitors minus one); use zero if there is only one visitor. Return visitor_id, country, purchase_revenue rounded to two decimals, percentile_fraction rounded to four decimals, ordered by unrounded purchase revenue and then visitor_id ascending.
expected_sql:
WITH totals AS
    (SELECT v.id AS visitor_id,
            v.country,
            COALESCE(SUM(CASE
                             WHEN e.event_type = 'purchase' THEN e.revenue
                             ELSE 0
                         END), 0) AS purchase_revenue
     FROM visitors AS v
     LEFT JOIN sessions AS s ON s.visitor_id = v.id
     LEFT JOIN EVENTS AS e ON e.session_id = s.id
     GROUP BY v.id,
              v.country)
SELECT visitor_id,
       country,
       ROUND(purchase_revenue, 2) AS purchase_revenue,
       ROUND(PERCENT_RANK() OVER (
                                  ORDER BY purchase_revenue), 4) AS percentile_fraction
FROM totals
ORDER BY totals.purchase_revenue,
         visitor_id;

question: Find unordered pairs of bidders who have both bid on at least two distinct open listings. Return smaller_bidder_id, larger_bidder_id, and shared_listing_count, ordered by those two IDs. Multiple bids by one bidder on one listing count only once.
expected_sql:
SELECT b1.bidder_id AS smaller_bidder_id,
       b2.bidder_id AS larger_bidder_id,
       COUNT(DISTINCT b1.listing_id) AS shared_listing_count
FROM bids b1
JOIN bids b2 ON b2.listing_id = b1.listing_id
AND b1.bidder_id < b2.bidder_id
JOIN listings l ON l.id = b1.listing_id
WHERE l.status = 'open'
GROUP BY b1.bidder_id,
         b2.bidder_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT b1.listing_id) >= 2
ORDER BY b1.bidder_id,
         b2.bidder_id;

question: Find unordered participant pairs with exactly the same set of mandatory questions answered with non-NULL scores. Require that each participant answered at least one mandatory question. Return smaller_participant_id and larger_participant_id, ordered by both IDs.
expected_sql:
WITH answered AS
    (SELECT r.participant_id,
            r.question_id
     FROM responses r
     JOIN questions q ON q.id = r.question_id
     WHERE q.required = 1
         AND r.score IS NOT NULL)
SELECT p1.id AS smaller_participant_id,
       p2.id AS larger_participant_id
FROM participants p1
JOIN participants p2 ON p1.id < p2.id
WHERE EXISTS
        (SELECT 1
         FROM answered a
         WHERE a.participant_id = p1.id)
    AND EXISTS
        (SELECT 1
         FROM answered a
         WHERE a.participant_id = p2.id)
    AND NOT EXISTS
        (SELECT question_id
         FROM answered
         WHERE participant_id = p1.id
         EXCEPT SELECT question_id
         FROM answered
         WHERE participant_id = p2.id)
    AND NOT EXISTS
        (SELECT question_id
         FROM answered
         WHERE participant_id = p2.id
         EXCEPT SELECT question_id
         FROM answered
         WHERE participant_id = p1.id)
ORDER BY p1.id,
         p2.id;

question: For each registered participant group, compute the percentage of mandatory question-participant combinations that have a non-NULL score. The denominator is all registered participants in the group times the total number of mandatory questions; skips and missing responses are incomplete. Return group_name (Unassigned for NULL) and completion_percent rounded to two decimals, ordered by group_name. Use NULL if there are no mandatory questions.
expected_sql:
SELECT COALESCE(p.group_name, 'Unassigned') AS group_name,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(
                             (SELECT COUNT(*)
                              FROM responses r
                              JOIN questions q ON q.id = r.question_id
                              WHERE r.participant_id = p.id
                                  AND q.required = 1
                                  AND r.score IS NOT NULL)) / NULLIF(COUNT(*) *
                                                                         (SELECT COUNT(*)
                                                                          FROM questions
                                                                          WHERE required = 1), 0), 2) AS completion_percent
FROM participants p
GROUP BY COALESCE(p.group_name, 'Unassigned')
ORDER BY group_name;

question: Compute league points for every team from completed matches: 3 per win, 1 per draw, 0 per loss. Return team_id, name, and points, including 0 for teams without completed matches. Order by points descending, then team_id.
expected_sql:
WITH earned AS
    (SELECT home_team_id AS team_id,
            CASE
                WHEN home_score > away_score THEN 3
                WHEN home_score = away_score THEN 1
                ELSE 0
            END AS points
     FROM matches
     WHERE status = 'completed'
     UNION ALL SELECT away_team_id AS team_id,
                      CASE
                          WHEN away_score > home_score THEN 3
                          WHEN away_score = home_score THEN 1
                          ELSE 0
                      END AS points
     FROM matches
     WHERE status = 'completed')
SELECT t.id AS team_id,
       t.name,
       COALESCE(SUM(e.points), 0) AS points
FROM teams t
LEFT JOIN earned e ON e.team_id = t.id
GROUP BY t.id,
         t.name
ORDER BY points DESC,

question: For each team that has won a completed match, identify the strongest opponent it defeated. Strength is that opponent's total league points from all completed matches (3 for a win, 1 for a draw, 0 for a loss). Choose the lowest opponent ID if points tie. Return team_id, opponent_id, and opponent_points, ordered by team_id. Count an opponent once even if defeated repeatedly.
expected_sql:
WITH outcomes AS
    (SELECT home_team_id AS team_id,
            away_team_id AS opponent_id,
            CASE
                WHEN home_score > away_score THEN 3
                WHEN home_score = away_score THEN 1
                ELSE 0
            END AS points
     FROM matches
     WHERE status = 'completed'
     UNION ALL SELECT away_team_id,
                      home_team_id,
                      CASE
                          WHEN away_score > home_score THEN 3
                          WHEN away_score = home_score THEN 1
                          ELSE 0
                      END
     FROM matches
     WHERE status = 'completed'),
     standings AS
    (SELECT team_id,
            SUM(points) AS points
     FROM outcomes
     GROUP BY team_id),
     defeated AS
    (SELECT DISTINCT o.team_id,
                     o.opponent_id,
                     s.points AS opponent_points
     FROM outcomes o
     JOIN standings s ON s.team_id = o.opponent_id
     WHERE o.points = 3)
SELECT d.team_id,
       d.opponent_id,
       d.opponent_points
FROM defeated d
WHERE NOT EXISTS
        (SELECT 1
         FROM defeated d2
         WHERE d2.team_id = d.team_id
             AND (d2.opponent_points > d.opponent_points
                  OR (d2.opponent_points = d.opponent_points
                      AND d2.opponent_id < d.opponent_id)))
ORDER BY d.team_id;

question: For every experiment, return experiment_id, name, run_count, completed_runs, and failed_runs, in that order. Include experiments without runs with zero counts; running runs count only toward run_count. Sort by experiment_id ascending.

question: For every run, return run_id and target_coverage_percent, in that order, sorted by run_id. Coverage is 100 times the number of distinct target metrics with at least one non-NULL reading for that run divided by the number of defined metrics with non-NULL targets. Include all statuses and runs without readings, use zero coverage when no target is measured, return NULL if there are no target metrics, and round percentages to two decimals.
expected_sql:
SELECT r.id AS run_id,
       ROUND(100.0 *
                 (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT x.metric)
                  FROM measurements AS x
                  JOIN metrics AS m ON m.name = x.metric
                  WHERE x.run_id = r.id
                      AND x.value IS NOT NULL
                      AND m.target IS NOT NULL) / NULLIF(
                                                             (SELECT COUNT(*)
                                                              FROM metrics
                                                              WHERE target IS NOT NULL), 0), 2) AS target_coverage_percent
FROM runs AS r
ORDER BY run_id;

question: Find completed runs that have at least one non-NULL reading for every defined metric whose target is non-NULL. If there are no target metrics, all completed runs qualify. Return run_id and experiment_id, in that order, sorted by run_id ascending.

FROM runs AS r
WHERE r.status = 'completed'

question: Compare treatment and control yield for each experiment using completed runs only. First average non-NULL yield readings within each run, then average those run means within each variant so runs have equal weight. Ignore runs with no known yield and include only experiments with a known mean for both variants. Return experiment_id, control_mean, treatment_mean, and percent_change, in that order. Percent change is 100 times (treatment minus control) divided by control; return NULL when control is zero. Round all three calculated values to two decimals and sort by experiment_id.
expected_sql:
WITH run_means AS
    (SELECT r.id AS run_id,
            r.experiment_id,
            r.variant,
            AVG(x.value) AS mean_yield
     FROM runs AS r
     JOIN measurements AS x ON x.run_id = r.id
     WHERE r.status = 'completed'
         AND x.metric = 'yield'
         AND x.value IS NOT NULL
     GROUP BY r.id,
              r.experiment_id,
              r.variant),
     experiment_means AS
    (SELECT experiment_id,
            AVG(CASE
                    WHEN variant = 'control' THEN mean_yield
                END) AS control_mean,
            AVG(CASE
                    WHEN variant = 'treatment' THEN mean_yield
                END) AS treatment_mean
     FROM run_means
     GROUP BY experiment_id)
SELECT experiment_id,
       ROUND(control_mean, 2) AS control_mean,
       ROUND(treatment_mean, 2) AS treatment_mean,
       ROUND(100.0 * (treatment_mean - control_mean) / NULLIF(control_mean, 0), 2) AS percent_change
FROM experiment_means
WHERE control_mean IS NOT NULL
    AND treatment_mean IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY experiment_id;

question: For each metric with a non-NULL target, find the completed runs whose mean non-NULL reading is closest to that target. Average repeated readings within a run, omit runs without a known reading, compare absolute distances before rounding, and keep all tied runs. Return metric, run_id, mean_value, and distance, in that order. Round mean_value and distance to two decimals and sort by metric ascending, then run_id ascending.
expected_sql:
WITH run_means AS
    (SELECT m.name AS metric,
            r.id AS run_id,
            AVG(x.value) AS mean_value,
            ABS(AVG(x.value) - m.target) AS distance
     FROM metrics AS m
     JOIN measurements AS x ON x.metric = m.name
     JOIN runs AS r ON r.id = x.run_id
     WHERE m.target IS NOT NULL
         AND x.value IS NOT NULL
         AND r.status = 'completed'
     GROUP BY m.name,
              m.target,
              r.id)
SELECT a.metric,
       a.run_id,
       ROUND(a.mean_value, 2) AS mean_value,
       ROUND(a.distance, 2) AS distance
FROM run_means AS a
WHERE NOT EXISTS
        (SELECT 1
         FROM run_means AS b
         WHERE b.metric = a.metric
             AND b.distance < a.distance)
ORDER BY a.metric,
         a.run_id;

question: For every project, return project_id, name, known_cost, and unpriced_hours, in that order. Include all task statuses and dates. Known cost is the sum of hours times billed_rate for entries with a non-NULL rate; unpriced hours are hours with a NULL rate. Use zero for missing totals and projects with no work, round both totals to two decimals, and sort by project_id ascending.
expected_sql:
SELECT p.id AS project_id,
       p.name,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(e.hours * e.billed_rate), 0), 2) AS known_cost,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(CASE
                              WHEN e.billed_rate IS NULL THEN e.hours
                              ELSE 0
                          END), 0), 2) AS unpriced_hours
FROM projects AS p
LEFT JOIN tasks AS t ON t.project_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN time_entries AS e ON e.task_id = t.id
GROUP BY p.id,
         p.name
ORDER BY project_id;

question: Find tasks whose own status is not done and whose direct prerequisites are all done. Tasks without prerequisites qualify. Return task_id and title, in that order, sorted by task_id ascending. Consider only direct prerequisites, regardless of the task due date or assignee.

question: List every direct or indirect prerequisite of task 5. Follow dependency edges recursively, return each prerequisite only once even if reachable through multiple paths, and exclude task 5 itself. Return task_id and title, in that order, sorted by task_id ascending; include prerequisites of any status.
expected_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE prerequisites(task_id) AS
    (SELECT depends_on
     FROM dependencies
     WHERE task_id = 5
     UNION SELECT d.depends_on
     FROM dependencies AS d
     JOIN prerequisites AS p ON d.task_id = p.task_id)
SELECT t.id AS task_id,
       t.title
FROM prerequisites AS p
JOIN tasks AS t ON t.id = p.task_id
WHERE t.id <> 5
ORDER BY task_id;

question: Find the task with the greatest known cost within each project, keeping all tied tasks and omitting projects with no tasks. Include every task status and date. A task known cost is the sum of hours times non-NULL billed_rate, or zero when it has no priced entries. Compare unrounded costs. Return project_id, task_id, title, and known_cost, in that order, round known_cost to two decimals, and sort by project_id then task_id ascending.
expected_sql:
WITH task_costs AS
    (SELECT t.project_id,
            t.id AS task_id,
            t.title,
            COALESCE(SUM(e.hours * e.billed_rate), 0) AS known_cost
     FROM tasks AS t
     LEFT JOIN time_entries AS e ON e.task_id = t.id
     GROUP BY t.project_id,
              t.id,
              t.title)
SELECT a.project_id,
       a.task_id,
       a.title,
       ROUND(a.known_cost, 2) AS known_cost
FROM task_costs AS a
WHERE NOT EXISTS
        (SELECT 1
         FROM task_costs AS b
         WHERE b.project_id = a.project_id
             AND b.known_cost > a.known_cost)
ORDER BY a.project_id,
         a.task_id;

question: For every project, return project_id, task_count, dependency_edge_count, and total_hours, in that order. Count each task once, count each direct dependency edge once for the project owning its dependent task, and sum each time entry once. Include all statuses and dates, preserve projects without tasks with zero totals, round hours to two decimals, and sort by project_id ascending.
expected_sql:
WITH task_totals AS
    (SELECT project_id,
            COUNT(*) AS task_count
     FROM tasks
     GROUP BY project_id),
     dependency_totals AS
    (SELECT t.project_id,
            COUNT(*) AS dependency_edge_count
     FROM tasks AS t
     JOIN dependencies AS d ON d.task_id = t.id
     GROUP BY t.project_id),
     time_totals AS
    (SELECT t.project_id,
            SUM(e.hours) AS total_hours
     FROM tasks AS t
     JOIN time_entries AS e ON e.task_id = t.id
     GROUP BY t.project_id)
SELECT p.id AS project_id,
       COALESCE(t.task_count, 0) AS task_count,
       COALESCE(d.dependency_edge_count, 0) AS dependency_edge_count,
       ROUND(COALESCE(h.total_hours, 0), 2) AS total_hours
FROM projects AS p
LEFT JOIN task_totals AS t ON t.project_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN dependency_totals AS d ON d.project_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN time_totals AS h ON h.project_id = p.id
ORDER BY project_id;
